newsitem.title: POLAND: Merrill lowers BRE to "neutral" rating.
newsitem.headline: Merrill lowers BRE to "neutral" rating.

text.p: Merrill Lynch in London has lowered its long-term opinion on shares in Polish Bank Rozwoju Exportu SA (BRE) to "neutral" from "accumulate" due to BRE's September gain of about 18 percent, Merrill said in a report.
The report dated September 30 said BRE's bourse price then of 95 zlotys had exceeded Merrill's 1996 price objective for BRE of 85 zlotys.
BRE closed on the Warsaw bourse on Tuesday at 98 zlotys.

"While we find the shares somewhat richly priced for building a new position, we believe that investors with an existing position in BRE will continue to be rewarded by above average performance," the report said.
It said the above average performance would be supported by average earnings growth of 14 percent through the year 2000 and an improving risk profile.

Merrill also said the bank's fundamental prospects remained strong, marked by first-half loans up 17 percent from December 1995, and that BRE was on track to match Merrill's net income forecast of 140 million zlotys, meaning real growth of 13 percent from last year.
"Hence we recommend holding, rather than reducing, current positions in BRE," Merrill said.
